name: GitHub isolated-branch exchange with immutable-SHA custody and dual-transport read-back
independence_argument: This route uses an authenticated GitHub identity over the git wire protocol and the GitHub REST API. It does not use the Cursor MCP surface and survives a total loss of the Cursor control plane, because the repository — not the provider — is canonical.

bounded_work_unit.description: Create an isolated branch from a resolved immutable source SHA, produce a hash-bound evidence bundle, publish it, then re-fetch and compare every byte against the remote.

result_retrieval.addressing_scheme: immutable commit SHA -> tree path -> blob SHA-1 -> content bytes

transports.method: git fetch --no-tags origin <sha> followed by git cat-file -p <sha>:<path>

result_retrieval.comparison_rule: Every manifested bundle file must be byte-identical to the remote object under both transports. Any single differing byte sets REMOTE_READBACK_MISMATCH and blocks the qualified state.

stable_locators.resume_checkpoint: resolve the branch head with git ls-remote and act only on the resolved immutable SHA
SO-02 source head at qualification start

failure_injection.injected: Structural write attempts against protected targets: the selected SO-02 source branch, the PR #9 PO-03 branch, a cursor/po03-* branch, main, the PR #6 and PR #7 branches, workstreams/po03/**, global state/** and an unscoped workflow file.
failure_injection.observed: Every attempt is refused by orchqual guard_paths before any write occurs; refusals are asserted by executable tests in tests/test_orchqual.py.

limits_and_honest_gaps: The GitHub identity available to this runtime is read-only for pull-request creation through the CLI; PR creation is performed through the runtime's own pull-request tool. Branch pushes are unaffected.
Remote read-back proves custody of what was pushed. It cannot prove intent; independent acceptance remains a separate, non-self-issued step.
